method: Small AR drafter proposes gamma tokens; target scores them in one pass; modified rejection sampling
upside: Target verifies gamma tokens in one memory-bound pass, so latency drops with no change to the output distribution
method_downside: Separate drafter runs gamma sequential passes and keeps its own KV cache; drafter must share the target tokenizer; rejected tokens waste target FLOPs (more total arithmetic), which hurts once compute-bound
memory: Separate drafter (T5-small 77M to T5-large for T5-XXL) + its KV cache (unv.)
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; acceptance rate alpha per pair/task (e.g. ~0.75 EnDe T5-small, unv.)
speed: 2-3x vs T5X on T5-XXL 11B, TPU-v4, bs1 (unv.); ~3.4x EnDe T=0 with T5-small (unv.)
datasets: WMT EnDe, CNN/DM (T5); lm1b (GPT-like 97M); LaMDA 137B dialog (alpha only)

method: Independent derivation of lossless speculative sampling with a separately trained drafter
upside: Same draft-then-verify gain; works for greedy and nucleus sampling
method_downside: Drafter is a separate 4B model trained for the target (same tokenizer), with its own weights and KV; drafting is sequential so drafter latency grows with K; speedup plateaus or regresses as K grows (stated)
memory: 4B drafter (~8 GB bf16, est.) + its KV cache
speed: 2-2.5x on Chinchilla 70B, distributed TPU setup (abstract); per-task numbers not captured

method: KD of drafter on on-policy (drafter-generated) data with divergence chosen per task (FKL/RKL/JSD/TVD)
upside: Aligns drafter to target distribution where drafter actually samples, raising block efficiency
method_downside: Training needs target logits for every drafter-generated token (target forward in the training loop); best divergence is task/decoding dependent, so per-setting tuning; drafter stays a separate model + KV
memory: Separate drafter (T5-Small 77M for T5-XL 3B; 33M for 234M decoder) + its KV
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; block efficiency figures only
speed: +10-45% over standard SD; lossy SD 6-10x latency cut; TPUv4, bs1
datasets: XSum, CNN/DM, WMT EnDe, GSM8K, LM1B, BigBenchHard (transfer)

method: Continually distill the drafter on live query traffic using verification results (rejected tokens)
upside: Drafter tracks the actual query distribution, raising acceptance without offline data collection
method_downside: Online training runs on serving GPUs (gradients, optimizer state, target logits buffer) and assumes idle compute; drafter weights change during serving, so behavior drifts and replicas can diverge; separate drafter + KV
memory: LLaMA-160M drafter + its KV + training state (grads, optimizer) on serving GPU (est.)
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; token acceptance rate +0.1 to +0.65
speed: 1.22-3.06x latency reduction (README/abstract); hardware not captured
llama_results: Vicuna-7B target with LLaMA-160M drafter among pairs; per-model numbers not captured
datasets: Spider, GSM8K, Code-Search-Python, Alpaca-finance; T5 experiments

method: Pretrain 115M drafter, build distillation set from target generations, fine-tune with TVD++ loss
upside: Small dedicated drafter aligned to a chat-tuned target via a variance-reduced TV objective
method_downside: Drafter must be pretrained from scratch with target tokenizer (32 A100 pretraining) plus target-generated distillation data; separate model + KV; fine-tuned drafter can lose to base drafter on OOD tasks (stated)
memory: 115M drafter (4 layers, d=1024) + its KV
accepted_tokens: block efficiency up to 2.3 (gamma=3, Llama 2 Chat 7B); CNN/DM 2.29 -> 2.4
speed: up to 2.4x vs AR, reported as MBSU (memory-bound speedup), not wall-clock
llama_results: Llama 2 Chat 7B: block eff. up to 2.3, up to 2.4x MBSU

method: Selective KD: train a reference drafter, then distill only on top-k% tokens by loss gap (default k=0.4)
upside: Drafter spends its small capacity on tokens it can match, raising acceptance
method_downside: Needs an extra reference-model distillation run (two-phase training); drafter is trained on only ~40% of tokens, so it is deliberately weak on hard tokens; separate drafter + KV
memory: Separate drafter (Pythia-31M, CodeGen-350M, Qwen2.5-0.5B) + KV; reference model is training-only
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; acceptance rate e.g. GSM8K 62.6% vs 57.6% (Pythia 31M->1.4B), MBPP 65.1% vs 49.9% (optimal)
speed: +6-27% tokens/s over DistillSpec (A100, greedy); e.g. MBPP 0.69 -> 0.57 s/sentence
llama_results: EAGLE integration, Vicuna-7B-v1.3 MT-Bench: 63.48 -> 68.21 tok/s, acceptance 75.3% -> 76.3%
datasets: GSM8K, Alpaca, MBPP, CNN/DM, XSum; MT-Bench (EAGLE integration)

method: Log-linear laws for acceptance vs drafter pretraining tokens, capacity and batch; builds multi-layer EAGLE-style Scylla drafter
upside: Pretraining the drafter on ~10B tokens and adding layers raises acceptance well above EAGLE-2
method_downside: Bigger multi-layer drafter (up to 5 layers) costs more per draft step; needs ~10B-token drafter pretraining; EAGLE-style, so tied to target features and retrained per target
memory: 138M / 275M / 413M drafter (1/2/5 layers) + its KV
accepted_tokens: tau 6.45 vs EAGLE-2 3.94 (Vicuna-7B, T=0); 5.22 vs 4.06 (Qwen2.5-7B, T=0)
speed: ~2x throughput over EAGLE-2 on Qwen2.5-72B, 4 GPUs, bs64 (2150 vs 980 tok/s)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/DM, Natural Questions

method: K extra FFN heads on last hidden state predict t+2..t+K+1 independently; tree attention; Medusa-1 frozen, Medusa-2 joint
upside: No separate model or KV; heads reuse target features and train cheaply (5 h on A100 for 7B)
method_downside: Heads predict each offset independently, so later heads ignore earlier choices and acceptance decays with depth; each head has its own vocab-size projection; Medusa-2 changes backbone weights and typical acceptance is lossy
memory: not reported; ~0.15B per head at 7B (d x d ResBlock + d x 32k head), ~0.74B for 5 heads (est.)
quality: lossless for Medusa-1 greedy; typical acceptance lossy: MT-Bench score delta -0.14 to +0.05
speed: Medusa-1 2.18x, Medusa-2 2.83x (Vicuna-7B, A100, bs1, MT-Bench)
llama_results: Vicuna-7B M1 2.18x, M2 2.83x; Vicuna-13B M1 2.33x, M2 2.83x; Vicuna-33B M2 2.35x (MT-Bench, bs1)

method: Draft heads conditioned on previously drafted tokens; Hydra++ adds 4-layer MLP heads, extra decoder layer, teacher distillation
upside: Sequential dependency fixes Medusa's independent-head problem, raising acceptance ~20%
method_downside: Heads now run sequentially (one call per draft position), so drafting latency grows with depth; Hydra++ extra decoder layer adds its own KV cache; retrained per target
memory: not reported; larger than Medusa heads (4-layer MLP per head + 1 decoder layer ~0.2B at 7B, est.)
quality: lossless (greedy); typical sampling eps=0.15 matches base quality (stated)
speed: Hydra++ 2.70x vs AR, 1.27x vs Medusa (Vicuna-7B, A100-40GB, bs1); 1.63x at bs8
datasets: MT-Bench; summarization and RAG tasks (names not captured)

method: One-layer AR drafter over target second-to-top features plus token shifted one step; static tree
upside: Drafter reads target features, so one small layer suffices; feature-level AR resolves sampling uncertainty
method_downside: Needs target hidden states each round, so drafting cannot start before verification ends; drafter has its own (1-layer) KV cache; retrained per target (and per fine-tune)
memory: 0.24B / 0.37B / 0.56B / 0.99B drafter for 7B/13B/33B/70B + 1-layer KV
speed: 3.03x (Vicuna-13B, bs1, T=0, MT-Bench); ~2x throughput at max batch

method: Context-aware dynamic draft tree using drafter confidence as acceptance proxy; reranking; reuses EAGLE drafter
upside: Spends draft budget where acceptance is likely; no retraining over EAGLE
method_downside: Relies on drafter being well calibrated (stated); tree shape changes per step, which breaks static CUDA graphs and batching; still needs target features and per-target drafter
memory: same as EAGLE (0.24B for 7B) + 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: tau 4.83 (Vicuna-13B, T=0); 4.53 (LLaMA3-Instruct-8B, T=0); dataset column ambiguous in extraction
speed: 4.26x (Vicuna-13B, T=0, bs1); 3.80x at T=1
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/DM, Natural Questions

method: Direct token prediction (no feature loss), fused low/mid/high target features, training-time test
upside: Fused multi-layer features plus training on its own outputs let acceptance keep scaling with training data
method_downside: Needs low/mid/high hidden states from the target each round, so drafter is tied to target internals and retrained per target; training-time test multiplies training cost; gain collapses at batch ~56 as verification becomes compute-bound
memory: not reported; ~0.4B for 8B target (1 decoder layer + 3d->d fusion FC + 32k draft-vocab head, est.) + 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: not captured from EAGLE-3 itself; GTO re-run: tau 6.07 (LLaMA-3.1-8B, T=0), 6.80 (Vicuna-13B)
speed: 5.58x (Vicuna-13B, bs1, T=0); vLLM 1.75x bs2 -> 1.01x bs56 (chain 2, no tree)
llama_results: T=0: Vicuna-13B 5.58x, LLaMA-3.1-8B 4.40x, LLaMA-3.3-70B 4.11x, R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B 4.05x; T=1 3.07x (L3.1-8B)

method: Top-K ranking distillation plus multi-step context alignment (train on drafter's own features) over EAGLE-2
upside: Drafter sees its own features in training, reducing train/inference mismatch at no inference cost
method_downside: Multi-step (3-step) alignment multiplies training cost vs EAGLE; needs target top-K logits during training; inherits EAGLE-2 per-target drafter and target-feature dependency
memory: same as EAGLE-2 drafter (~0.24B for 7B, est.) + 1-layer KV
speed: 4.05x (LLaMA3-Instruct-70B, H800, bs1, T=0)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K (README DeepSeek runs add Alpaca, QA, Summarization)

method: Token-alignable training (mask misaligned tokens) plus draft model with token-guided fusion and token-enhanced head
upside: Fixes feature/token misalignment between training and decoding, lengthening accepted drafts
method_downside: Larger drafter than EAGLE (TGF expanded to 11008, dual heads); multi-step training (150-600 A100-h vs HASS 130-500); masking removes loss signal on misaligned (hard) tokens
memory: 0.41B / 0.42B / 0.65B / 2.07B drafter for 7B/8B/13B/70B + its KV
speed: 3.28x (LLaMA3-8B, A100 80G, bs1, T=0); README claims up to 4.2x

method: Semi-AR drafter (k tokens per pass) with coupled sequential glancing distillation; custom decoding tree
upside: Fewer drafter passes per draft block than a pure AR drafter
method_downside: Tokens inside a block are predicted without seeing each other, lowering acceptance (stated; CSGD only partly fixes it); ~2-layer drafter heavier than EAGLE's; needs target features, retrained per target
memory: not reported; ~2 transformer-layer equivalent (LSTM + attention + MLP), ~0.4B for 7B (est.) + KV
speed: 2.91-3.51x on Vicuna and LLaMA2-Chat (hardware/bs not captured)

method: RNN drafter conditioned on target hidden states; beam search drafting; dynamic tree attention dedups prefixes; KD from target
upside: Tiny recurrent drafter is cheap per step and runs on-device (MLX)
method_downside: Beam search (width up to 45) multiplies drafter and verification work, which hurts at batch>1; needs target hidden states; non-greedy implementation may not match the distribution exactly (README)
memory: not reported (lightweight RNN drafter + per-beam state)
quality: lossless at T=0; T>0 implementation may not match distribution (README)
speed: 2.80x (Vicuna-7B/13B, H100, PyTorch, bs1, greedy); MLX M2 Ultra 13B 1.94x (abstract: up to 2.3x)

method: Sampling-free draft-tree reward plus group-based policy optimization of the drafter
upside: Training objective matches tree decoding, so drafter optimizes accepted length of the tree, not per-token loss
method_downside: Training builds and evaluates grouped draft trees (two phases, 200-900 GPU-h, stated); reward is tied to one tree policy; starts from an EAGLE-3 drafter, so inherits its target-feature dependency and per-target retraining
memory: same as EAGLE-3 drafter (initialized from it); no extra inference memory
speed: 3.73x (LLaMA-3.1-8B, A100 80GB, bs1, T=0); +7.7% over EAGLE-3

method: Hybrid KL + total-variation loss with adaptive schedule, directly optimizing acceptance rate
upside: Loss targets acceptance itself, helping low-capacity drafters most; drop-in for any drafter type
method_downside: TV term needs the full target distribution per training token; objective models chain sampling, not tree verification; fixed per-head aggregation and scheduler hyperparameters (stated)
memory: none beyond the drafter it trains (EAGLE-3, Medusa, MLP speculator, MTP)
accepted_tokens: tau 3.84 vs 3.75 KL (LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3, T=0, MT-Bench, chain); 3.48 vs 3.39 at T=1
speed: 2.62x MT-Bench, 3.35x HumanEval (LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3, vLLM 0.11, bs1, T=0)
llama_results: LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3: tau 3.84 (T=0), speed 2.62x MT-Bench; LLaMA-3.3-70B also tested (numbers not captured)

method: On-policy distillation with target-assisted rollouts, error-position replay, acceptance-aware loss weighting
upside: Drafter trains on its own rollouts, closing exposure bias at deep positions
method_downside: Training needs the target in the loop for rollouts (RL-style verl stack, teacher inference memory); per-target retraining; main recipe is on a DFlash block drafter, so inherits its target-feature dependency
memory: not reported (DFlash b16 or EAGLE-3 drafter, same as base drafter)
speed: mean 4.86x (Qwen3-4B, T=0 thinking), 4.89x (Qwen3-8B); hardware/bs not captured
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, MBPP, HumanEval, SWE-Lite, MT-Bench

method: Simulate target verification at each training step; accept/reject patterns supervise via verification head and per-position weights
upside: Drafter learns where verification actually rejects, raising accepted length at no inference cost
method_downside: Each training step runs a simulated verification (target forward), raising training cost; verification head is training-only; drafter still per-target
memory: none beyond base drafter (EAGLE-3 or DFlash); verification head training-only
accepted_tokens: tau 6.78 vs 6.28 (Qwen3-4B EAGLE-3, T=0); DFlash 6.08 vs 5.73
speed: 4.39x vs 4.07x (Qwen3-4B EAGLE-3, A100 80GB, bf16, HF, T=0)
llama_results: LLaMA-3.1-8B: EAGLE-3 tau +2.5%, speed +3.8%; DFlash tau +3.8%, speed +3.4%
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Online learning (dynamic regret) evolves drafters from verification feedback; Ens-EAGLE(-3), Opt-Hydra, Online-LR
upside: Drafter adapts to live traffic with a regret bound linked to speedup
method_downside: Ens-EAGLE keeps N=O(log T) drafter copies with different learning rates (memory xN); online updates use serving GPUs and drafter drifts; Online-LR variant is step-level and lossy
memory: Ens: N=O(log T) drafter copies + optimizer state (not quantified); Opt-Hydra: Hydra heads + momentum state
quality: lossless (token-level variants); Online-LR lossy (MMLU acc 84.52% reported)
speed: 1.55x (Opt-Hydra, Vicuna-7B); 1.84x (Vicuna-13B); 4x A800 80GB
llama_results: Vicuna-7B: Opt-Hydra 1.55x/tau 2.70, Ens-EAGLE 1.41x/2.01, Ens-EAGLE-3 1.26x/2.16; Vicuna-13B Opt-Hydra 1.84x/2.73
datasets: GSM8K, MATH, MMLU (math subset), Code-Search-Python, Spider, MBPP, Alpaca-finance

method: Drafter split into frozen shared and trainable private MoE experts; regenerate data with fine-tuned target; select high-value samples
upside: Re-aligns a drafter to a fine-tuned target with 27.5% of params and ~61% of retrain cost
method_downside: MoE drafter (shared + private experts + router) is larger than a plain EAGLE drafter; still needs the fine-tuned target to regenerate data and retrain the private part per fine-tune
memory: ~462 MB drafter, 127 MB trainable private part
speed: 3.06x vs ~2.88x (Math-7B, T=0, notes); PDF extract 3.27x, README 3.45x (inconsistent); 4x H200
datasets: Math: GSM8K, AIME24, SVAMP, MATH, MathQA; Code: HumanEval(+), APPS, BigCodeBench, MBPP; Medical: MedMCQA, MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU-clinical (repo)

method: Draft by skipping ~half of target layers (attn+MLP set found by Bayesian optimization); full model verifies
upside: No extra model or training; draft shares weights and KV with target
method_downside: Draft still runs ~50% of target depth per token, capping speedup; skip set searched offline per model (2.5-6 h BO) and static, so it degrades under task shift
memory: none (shared weights and KV; authors: no extra memory)
speed: 1.22-1.99x (A100, HF, bs1 implied); best 1.99x LLaMA-2-70B CNN/DM

method: Train with layer dropout + shared early-exit loss; early layers draft, remaining layers verify
upside: Draft and verifier share weights, LM head and KV cache, so no auxiliary model
method_downside: Needs layer-dropout/early-exit (continual) pretraining that changes base weights; draft quality capped by shallow exit layer; later fine-tuning can break exits
memory: none extra (single model, shared KV and exit head)
quality: lossless vs the LayerSkip-trained model (which differs from original checkpoint)
accepted_tokens: not reported in abstract (acceptance tracked in paper)
speed: up to 2.16x CNN/DM, 1.82x coding, 2.0x TOPv2 (hardware not recorded)
llama_results: Llama2-7B/13B, Llama 1.5B, Llama1-7B code (v1); later versions add Llama3 (unv.); up to 2.16x

method: Fixed shallow sub-network (layer 2-3) + trained 1-attention adapter drafts; second early exit stops drafting on low confidence
upside: Tiny adapter (67M vs Medusa 591M) reuses target's shallow layers and KV
method_downside: Adapter trained per target; draft quality capped by fixed shallow exit layer; drafting still runs the shallow sub-network sequentially per token
memory: 67M adapter (Vicuna-7B) + its 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: compression rate 1.41-2.22 by Spec-Bench subtask (Vicuna-7B, per fetched table)
speed: up to 1.68x Spec-Bench; avg 1.50x Vicuna-7B, 1.44x Vicuna-13B (V100, bs1 implied)
datasets: Spec-Bench (MT-Bench, translation, QA, summarization, math, RAG)

method: On-the-fly optimization of skipped-layer set from current context + confidence-based draft stopping; no training
upside: Plug-and-play; adapts skip set to task without offline search
method_downside: Skip-set optimization phase at inference (~2 min) and task-dependent sparsity; draft keeps ~half of layers so speedup capped; small models have little layer redundancy
memory: none (shared weights and KV)
llama_results: LLaMA-2-13B 1.28-1.53x (1.37x CNN/DM, 1.31x GSM8K, 1.53x TinyStories); LLaMA-2-70B 1.39-1.62x; CodeLLaMA-13B/34B tested
datasets: CNN/DM, GSM8K, TinyStories, HumanEval, WMT16 De-En

method: Re-select skipped layers every step via dynamic programming over hidden states from the last verify pass; no training
upside: Skip set tracks the context each step instead of a static or per-task set
method_downside: Per-step DP adds latency that eats most of the gain on small models (1.24x at 8B); depends on last verify's hidden states so drafting waits for verification; draft still deep
memory: none extra beyond cached hidden states of last verify (est.)
datasets: Spec-Bench (MT-Bench, translation, summarization, QA, math, RAG)

method: Picks exit layer and speculation length per context from tracked per-layer acceptance in LayerSkip-style self-SD
upside: Adapts draft depth and length to context with negligible runtime overhead
method_downside: Needs LayerSkip early-exit-trained checkpoints; exit choice relies on running acceptance stats, so it degrades on out-of-distribution prompts
memory: 0.52-2.26% memory overhead (LayerSkip 0.50-1.42%)
speed: 2.16-2.62x vs AR (A100/H100, bs1, greedy and T=0.6)
llama_results: LLaMA-3-8B 2.62x; LLaMA-2-7B 2.50x; LLaMA-2-70B 2.84x (as summarized); CodeLLaMA-7B 2.26x; also Llama-3.2-1B, 13B, CodeLlama-34B
datasets: CNN/DM, XSum, HumanEval, AQuA-RAT-CoT, GSM8K, WMT14 De-En

method: Per-layer lightweight predictor uses speculative (EAGLE) draft tokens as features to decide early exit
upside: Cuts per-token depth with tiny MLP predictors; works on cloud and PC engines
method_downside: Lossy early exit, output can differ from the full model; predictors trained per model and need an EAGLE draft model for features
memory: predictors ~416 KB (Llama2-7B); 0.9-1.4 GB total incl. EAGLE draft
quality: lossy: <1% accuracy drop reported (MMLU, CSQA, SST2, GSM8K)
speed: 2.25x cloud (A100 80GB vs HF), 2.43x PC (RTX 4060 laptop vs llama.cpp)
llama_results: Llama2-7B 2.25x cloud / 2.43x PC; Llama2-13B/70B 1.14x/1.12x over HF baseline component
datasets: MT-Bench, SUM, QA, Alpaca, GSM8K, HumanEval, MMLU, CommonsenseQA, SST2

method: Three levels on EE models: shallow layer (~1/8 depth) drafts, intermediate EE layer (~1/4) verifies tentatively, full model verifies periodically
upside: Cheap intermediate verifier rejects bad drafts early; KV and hidden states reused across all three levels
method_downside: Needs early-exit-trained models; tentatively accepted tokens can still be rolled back at final verification (wasted work); four coupled knobs (Nd, Ni, Ld, Li)
memory: negligible (<0.01% peak; shared KV and hidden states)
speed: avg 1.28x, up to 2.01x vs single-layer speculation (4x H100, HF, bs1 default, greedy); v1 best 2.08x
llama_results: Llama3-8B 1.84-2.08x; Llama2-70B 1.63-1.93x vs AR (as summarized); also Llama2-7B/13B, CodeLlama-34B

method: Self-draft with same architecture using 4-bit weights and hierarchical INT4 KV (upper/lower nibbles form INT8 for target)
upside: Draft KV is a bit-slice of the target KV, so no separate draft cache; targets KV-bound long context
method_downside: Gain only when KV loading dominates, shrinks for short prompts; draft runs full depth; needs custom quantized kernels
memory: draft KV shared with target (no extra); 4-bit draft weights (likely extra copy ~0.25x target weights, est.); ~1.3x memory saving vs sparse-KV drafts
speed: up to 2.49x (Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct, 32K ctx, bs1, A6000)

method: Draft with W4A4 activation+weight quantization, verify with W4A16 of the same 4-bit weights
upside: Single weight copy toggles between two activation modes; KV overwritten in place
method_downside: Lossless only relative to W4A16, not FP16; needs fast W4A4 and W4A16 kernels on the same weights; draft runs full depth
memory: none (shared weights and KV)
quality: lossless vs W4A16 (W4A4 alone loses e.g. 25-51% on GSM8K/MATH)
speed: avg 1.38x, up to 1.64x throughput vs W4A16 (Llama-2-7B, bs32, L20 48GB)
llama_results: Llama-2-7B up to 1.64x vs W4A16; Llama 3B/8B/13B tested
datasets: PIQA, WikiText-2, WinoGrande, GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, HumanEval, ShareGPT, LMsys-1K

method: Two-level hierarchy: Llama-68M with StreamingLLM cache drafts for target on retrieval-selected sparse KV (4K), which drafts for full-KV target
upside: Sparse-KV target is a strong cheap middle drafter for long context
method_downside: Needs a separate tiny draft model plus two speculation levels; gain needs long context where KV loading dominates; sparse retrieval cache rebuilt per prompt
memory: Llama-68M + 1K StreamingLLM KV + 4K retrieval KV (~3% of full)
speed: 2.31x A100 (Llama2-7B-128K, 122K prompt, bs1); 7.78x offloading on 2x RTX 4090
llama_results: Llama2-7B-128K 2.31x A100, 7.78x offload; Llama2-13B-128K 7.94x offload; LWM-Text-Chat-128K 7.37x

method: Self-speculation with StreamingLLM sparse KV drafter; shows SD helps at large batch for long sequences (cross-listed 5c)
upside: Draft KV is constant-size, so draft cost stays flat while target KV load grows with context and batch
method_downside: Draft runs full model depth, so gain only when KV loading dominates (long seq); fixed sparse window drops mid-context info and acceptance
memory: StreamingLLM draft KV 256-1024 tokens per sequence
speed: up to 2x LLaMA-2-7B-32K (32K, bs32), 1.84x LLaMA-3.1-8B (100K, bs32), 8x A100, greedy
llama_results: LLaMA-2-7B-32K up to 2x; LLaMA-3.1-8B 1.84x; TinyLlama-1.1B draft variant

method: Reframe greedy decoding as Jacobi/Gauss-Seidel fixed-point iteration over a block
upside: No model change or retraining
method_downside: Model not trained to guess future tokens, so few positions converge per iteration; gains small without parallel hardware
memory: none
speed: up to 38% faster than AR; ~2x with parallel resources (MT models)

method: Jacobi-style parallel n-gram generation (window W, n-gram N) plus verification branch over an n-gram pool
upside: No draft model or datastore; trades per-step FLOPs for fewer steps
method_downside: Spends 56-120x extra FLOPs per step, so it slows in compute-bound settings (large batch); Jacobi guesses from an untrained model have low hit rate
memory: none extra weights; n-gram pool (small, est.)
speed: up to 1.8x MT-Bench, 2.3x HumanEval (A100, bs1); 4x ClassEval with lookahead parallelism on 8 A100
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, ClassEval, XSum, CNN/DM, GSM8K

method: Fine-tune target on its own Jacobi trajectories so it reaches the fixed point in fewer iterations
upside: Jacobi decoding becomes effective with no draft model or extra parameters
method_downside: Modifies target weights, so output is not guaranteed equal to the original model; needs per-domain trajectory generation and training (2-30 A100 h)
memory: none at inference (target replaced by CLLM)
quality: lossless vs CLLM; vs original: near-no accuracy loss reported
accepted_tokens: not recorded (fast-forwarded tokens per iteration reported)
speed: 2.4-3.4x Jacobi, 2.5-3.6x with lookahead (A100, bs1)

method: Retrieve draft continuations from a datastore via suffix-array match on recent context; tree attention verify
upside: No draft model; drafts are real text from a large corpus
method_downside: Fixed datastore cannot match novel or in-context text (e.g. new variable names); CPU retrieval cost per step
memory: datastore 12 GB (UltraChat) or 27 GB (Stack) in CPU RAM
speed: Vicuna-7B MT-Bench 1.69x greedy / 1.62x nucleus; CodeLlama-7B HumanEval 2.36x / 2.12x (A6000, bs1)

method: String-match last n-gram (max 3) against the prompt and copy up to 10 following tokens as draft
upside: Zero cost drafting; strong when output copies input (summarization, RAG, editing)
method_downside: Can only copy text already in the prompt, so drafts fail on novel or open-ended output
memory: none
speed: avg ~2.4x on summarization and context QA (Mistral-7B-Instruct, A100 40GB); smaller on MT-Bench

method: Suffix trees over prompts and past outputs on CPU; adaptive speculation length by match frequency
upside: Very long drafts (6-8 tokens/step) on repetitive agentic workloads at no GPU cost
method_downside: Depends on repeated past outputs; on open-ended text drafts rarely match (1.75 tokens/step Spec-Bench), so needs a hybrid drafter
memory: suffix trees in CPU RAM (~6.15 GB per 572M cached tokens)
speed: 5.3x AgenticSQL, 2.5x SWE-Bench, hybrid 2.5x Spec-Bench (H100, bs1, vLLM)

method: Static (corpus) and dynamic (generated text) suffix automata give longest exact suffix match; falls back to generative drafter
upside: O(1) average match per step; combines with EAGLE-2 or Token Recycling
method_downside: Exact-match retrieval fails on novel text, so needs a fallback drafter chosen by a heuristic match-length rule
memory: suffix automata in CPU RAM, grows with corpus (not reported, est.)
speed: Spec-Bench 1.84x alone, 2.27x +Token Recycling, 2.58x +EAGLE-2; HumanEval 2.29x (A6000, bs1, greedy)

method: Keep adjacency matrix of past top-k candidates per token; BFS a draft tree; tree attention verify
upside: Training-free, <2 MB state, reuses otherwise discarded candidates
method_downside: Drafts limited to transitions seen as past top-k; static tree shape; acceptance drops as temperature rises
memory: <2 MB adjacency matrix

method: Draft only from LRU n-gram tables: dynamic table from generation plus frozen corpus table
upside: Tiny model-free drafter, cache policy adapts to locality
method_downside: Exact n-gram matching fails on novel text; six hand-set cache hyperparameters with no auto-tuning
memory: LRU n-gram tables (not reported; small, est.)
speed: avg 1.86x Vicuna-7B; 1.29-1.84x by task across 7B-33B (RTX 4090, bs1)

method: n independent heads on a shared trunk trained from scratch to predict n tokens; extra heads self-draft
upside: Draft comes for free from the pretrained model; 2.5 of 3 drafts accepted on code
method_downside: Requires MTP pretraining, cannot be added to existing checkpoints; heads predict offsets independently so later heads ignore earlier choices; hurts models below ~3B
memory: n-1 extra transformer-layer heads (7B, n=4: ~0.6B, est.)
accepted_tokens: ~2.5 of 3 drafts accepted on code (7B, n=4)
speed: 3.0x code, 2.7x text (7B, n=4); 6.4x byte-level n=8 (bs42, xFormers)

method: Sequential depth-1 MTP module trained with the model; reused as a 1-token speculative drafter
upside: Drafter trained jointly at pretraining, high second-token acceptance
method_downside: Depth 1 limits drafts to one extra token per step; must be built into pretraining
memory: 1 MTP module ~14B params on 671B model (unv.) + its KV
speed: ~1.8x TPS (unv.)

method: Fine-tune one shared-weight MTP head on self-distilled data, apply recursively for K=3; language-aware vocab compression
upside: Reuses the model's own MTP head for multi-step drafts at ~1 day training cost
method_downside: Recursive single head degrades with depth (acceptance ~80/56/36%); requires a base that ships an MTP module; vocab compression is language-specific
memory: 1 MTP head (already in MiMo) + its KV; compressed draft vocab
speed: 2.03x avg vs AR, 1.21x vanilla MTP (A10 24GB, SGLang, bs1, T=0)
datasets: 7 benchmarks, general NLP, math, code (names not recorded)

method: Append k mask tokens; gated LoRA active only on masks; 2-layer sampler head; quadratic decoding
upside: Keeps NTP outputs unchanged while the model predicts k future tokens in one pass
method_downside: Gated LoRA cannot be fused into base weights, adding latency; k mask tokens add compute per step; requires SFT-stage training
memory: gated LoRA + 2-layer sampler (size not reported; small, est.)
accepted_tokens: up to ~5x tokens/step math and code, ~2.5x chat (Tulu3-8B, k=8)
speed: 1.5-5.2x acceptance-based (not wall-clock), 8x A100 training
datasets: math, code, chat, knowledge tasks of Tulu3 eval (names not recorded)

method: Extra heads predict next k tokens in parallel; base model verifies, keep longest matching prefix
upside: k tokens proposed for the cost of one pass; no separate draft model
method_downside: each head predicts its offset independently, so later heads ignore earlier choices; heads share the base trunk, so proposal quality is capped by one hidden state
memory: not reported; (est.) k-1 extra output heads on the base model, no extra KV
quality: lossless (exact-match variant); lossy variants trade quality for up to 7x fewer iterations
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; up to 2x fewer decoding iterations lossless (MT)
speed: up to 4x wall-clock (MT and image super-resolution Transformers, greedy)

method: Small AR model adapted with mask tokens into a target-independent parallel drafter; COD training
upside: one drafter pass emits k tokens; one drafter serves a whole target family without retraining per target
method_downside: separate drafter model with its own KV that grows with context; target-independent drafter sees no target features, so it only works within one tokenizer family; mask positions predicted jointly without seeing each other's sampled tokens
memory: separate small LM: Llama3.2-1B (for LLaMA3), Qwen2.5-0.5B, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, plus its KV
speed: LLaMA3.1-8B avg 3.57x / 274.4 tok/s, HumanEval 4.08x / 311.5 tok/s; Qwen2.5-7B 4.87x (A100-40GB, bs1, T=0, Transformers+); abstract v4: 3.67x / 264.88 tok/s (versions conflict)
llama_results: LLaMA3.1-8B: HumanEval 4.08x, MATH500 3.35x, GSM8K 3.30x, avg 3.57x (Llama3.2-1B drafter)

method: Off-the-shelf diffusion LM drafts a token lattice; causal-consistency path search; adaptive draft length
upside: training-free: no drafter training or target alignment; many tokens per drafter pass
method_downside: unaligned dLLM drafter has no target features, so acceptance depends on dLLM-target agreement; path search over the lattice is a serial CPU/GPU step each round; full 7B drafter must share the GPU with the target
memory: Dream-7B drafter (~15 GB bf16, est.) plus its context processing
speed: up to 3x, mean 3.08x (Qwen2.5-32B, A100-80GB, T=0)
datasets: Spec-Bench: MT-Bench, WMT translation, CNN/DM, Natural Questions, GSM8K, RAG (DPR)

method: Discrete-diffusion drafter aligned with streak-distillation; test-time self-selection over several sampled drafts
upside: train objective targets long accepted streaks; parallel block drafting
method_downside: self-selection needs several drafter samples per round (extra drafter compute); block positions sampled from marginals, so drafts can be incoherent
memory: not reported (diffusion LM drafter, size not extracted)
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; later positions get 3.2x higher acceptance than AR drafter
speed: up to 5.5x avg over AR, +55% tok/s over prior baselines (Qwen2.5-14B/72B, Llama 13B/70B; hardware and T in appendix, not extracted)
llama_results: Llama 13B and 70B targets used; per-model numbers not extracted

method: dLLM drafter aligned to the AR target with a two-stage training pipeline
upside: block drafting with long possible accepts (up to 32 tokens) from one drafter call
method_downside: dLLM block positions independent given context; separate dLLM drafter retrained per target family
memory: not reported (dLLM drafter, size not stated)

method: EAGLE turned parallel: learnable shared hidden state fills future positions; long-context training via mask precomputation and sequence partitioning
upside: several tokens per drafter pass instead of one pass per token
method_downside: parallel positions share one learned hidden state, so later positions do not see earlier drafted tokens; drafter tied to target features (retrained per target); EAGLE drafter KV grows with context
memory: not reported; (est.) EAGLE-3-size single-layer drafter plus its KV
speed: 1.10-1.36x over AR EAGLE-3 (GPT-OSS 120B/20B, Qwen3-Coder-30B, vLLM; hardware/bs/T not extracted)
code: in vLLM; no standalone repo found

method: 5-layer block-diffusion drafter, block 16, one denoising step; target features from 5 layers injected into every draft layer's KV
upside: whole block in one drafter pass, so draft cost does not scale with block length; target features make a small drafter accurate
method_downside: positions conditionally independent within a block (product of marginals); needs fresh target features every round, so draft and verify serialize (ours: drafter ~16% of a round); block 16 caps accepted length at 16 per round
memory: not reported; (est.) ~1B drafter for Qwen3-8B (5 target-width layers + fc, shared embed/head) ~2 GB bf16; drafter KV ~5/36 of target KV, grows with context
accepted_tokens: tau 6.49 T=0, 5.48 T=1 (Qwen3-8B avg); 8.01 SGLang Math500 (ours: tau 5.85, Qwen3-8B, A100, HF)
speed: Qwen3-8B 4.86x T=0, 4.03x T=1 (H200, bs1, HF); SGLang B200 Math500 5.1x c=1 to 2.8x c=32 (ours: HF 4.37x; vLLM 4.84x, 2.69 ms/tok, A100 bs1)
llama_results: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, block 10, SGLang B200: GSM8K 2.4x at c=1 to 1.6x at c=32 (EAGLE-3 0.6x at c=32)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca; GPQA (thinking); LongBench subsets

method: DFlash plus grouped causal convolution per layer and a candidate selector (first-order Markov rerank of top-k)
upside: adds left-to-right information inside the block at small cost
method_downside: rerank is only first-order (predecessor/successor), so longer-range dependencies stay independent; still needs fresh target features each round
memory: not reported; (est.) DFlash-size drafter plus conv and codebook params
speed: not reported
llama_results: README lists Llama-3.1-8B as supported; no numbers found

method: Best-first heap builds top-B prefix tree from DFlash per-position marginals; one verify pass with ancestor mask
upside: recovers much of the joint structure lost by marginals without retraining; one drafter pass per round
method_downside: tree surrogate ignores dependencies (every node at a depth gets the same candidates); depth capped at block size 16; tree verify cost grows with nodes x batch and needs a dense SDPA mask (no FA2), plus a CPU heap sync each round
memory: no extra params; per round B+1 extra verify tokens, dense bf16 mask of N x (ctx+N), hidden states for all nodes
accepted_tokens: Qwen3-8B MATH-500 tau 10.73 vs DFlash 7.79 (T=0) (ours: DDTree-128 tau 8.1, Qwen3-8B, A100)
speed: Qwen3-8B MATH-500 7.52x vs DFlash 5.56x (H200, bs1, T=0, HF/SDPA; budget picked per cell) (ours: DDTree-128 HF 5.90x, A100)
datasets: MATH-500, GSM8K, AIME24, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench Lite, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Query-dependent best-first tree over DFlash marginals; path-confidence product as acceptance surrogate; roofline latency model sets budget online
upside: tree size matched to hardware cost per step without per-setting tuning
method_downside: surrogate is a product of marginals, ignores dependencies; budget controller needs hardware-calibrated latency profiles; inherits DFlash block cap and fresh-feature dependency
memory: no extra params beyond DFlash; tree verify tokens per round; controller overhead negligible
speed: Qwen3-8B 6.61x over AR, DFlash 4.56x (A100, bs1, T=0); avg 1.39x over DFlash, 2.45x over EAGLE-3
datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, Alpaca, MT-Bench, LongBench (English)

method: Per-round tree budget chosen to maximize tok/s from offline latency profile plus drafter confidence
upside: removes manual/oracle budget tuning; throughput unimodal in budget makes search cheap
method_downside: relies on a convex verify-cost assumption and an offline profile per hardware; tree still built from independent marginals; inherits block-16 depth cap
memory: no extra params; offline latency table; tree verify tokens per round
accepted_tokens: ~3.1-10.4 by dataset (Qwen3-4B/8B, T=0); Qwen3-4B MATH-500 10.37 vs DDTree-oracle 10.35
speed: Qwen3-4B MATH-500 4.53 ms/tok (= DDTree oracle) vs DFlash 5.93 ms/tok (A800, T=0)
datasets: MATH-500, GSM8K, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Target-distilled edge scores rate parent-child compatibility in diffusion draft trees; state-aware budget
upside: tree scoring conditions on the parent token, partly fixing marginal-only ranking
method_downside: drafting, tree construction and verification run sequentially each round; edge scores only pairwise, longer dependencies ignored; scorer distilled per target
memory: not reported; (est.) small (two linear projections + depth embeddings) on top of DFlash
accepted_tokens: Qwen3-8B GSM8K MAT 8.06 vs DDTree 8.18, DFlash 5.82
speed: 2.13-6.36x over AR; Qwen3-8B up to 6.17x (A100-80GB, bs1)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME24, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench, Alpaca

method: DFlash backbone plus GRU causal encoder over preceding tokens and low-rank residual logit correction
upside: restores left-to-right dependency at +5% params; keeps one backbone pass
method_downside: GRU runs sequentially over block positions, so a sequential step grows with block length; correction only helps when early positions are accepted; inherits fresh-feature dependency
memory: +56M params (+5.3%) on DFlash drafter (GRU 1024-d, rank 256)
speed: Qwen3-8B 5.49x vs DFlash 4.70x (A100, T=0, HF); up to 5.8x throughput in SGLang
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: SwiGLU layer on drafter state plus previous token approximates AR conditionals inside a DDTree-style tree
upside: parent-aware node distributions computed in M x gamma parallel evaluations, O(1) in depth
method_downside: only first-order conditioning (previous token); large trees conflict with production attention kernels (dense SDPA mask); inherits block cap
memory: not reported; (est.) one SwiGLU layer (~0.1B at 4096 hidden) on DFlash
speed: +9.1% over DDTree at B=64 (GH200, bs1, SDPA)

method: Drafter-1 confidence locates likely rejection points; variable-prefix drafter-2 re-drafts from top-K of them; branches verified together with cascade attention
upside: covers the likely failure point without a full tree
method_downside: two drafters run per round (second waits on the first); verify width grows with K branches; extra stages give diminishing returns (third stage -4% speed)
memory: not reported; (est.) two DFlash-size drafters (~2x drafter weights and draft KV)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Causal parallel draft head over fused hidden states gives branch-wise causal conditioning in one forward pass
upside: causal dependency along branches without per-token drafter passes
method_downside: not extracted (abstract only); (likely) tree verify cost grows with branches x batch
memory: not reported
speed: up to 9.64x MATH-500, 4.58x chat (H100, Qwen3 dense and MoE; bs/T not extracted)

method: DFlash-style parallel backbone plus light sequential module (low-rank Markov or RNN head); calibrated confidence head and load-aware scheduler pick verify length
upside: semi-AR refinement restores dependency cheaply; verify length shrinks under load
method_downside: sequential module runs once per draft position; scheduler depends on throughput profiling; drafter KV over full prefix grows with context (~2.5 GiB at 128K, derived from LongSpark's 406x)
memory: not reported; DFlash backbone + rank-256 head + linear confidence head; drafter state ~2.5 GiB at 128K (est.)
accepted_tokens: tau +16.3/18.4/18.3% vs DFlash on Qwen3-4B/8B/14B (absolute not extracted)
speed: DeepSeek-V4 production: 60-85% per-user speedup at matched throughput

method: Lightweight low-rank causal refiner reranks diffusion-draft candidates through parallel Jacobi iterations
upside: reaches sequential fixed point in K << block size parallel passes
method_downside: Jacobi iterations add K refiner passes to every round; refiner conditions on drafter candidates, so it cannot recover tokens outside them
memory: not reported; (est.) small, rank-256 refiner on DFlash
accepted_tokens: +18-56% vs DFlash at T=0, +19-58% at T=1 (Qwen3-8B)
speed: ~1.3x (up to 1.7x) over DFlash T=0, ~1.46x T=1 (Qwen3-8B, H200)
datasets: 7 math, code and chat benchmarks (not enumerated)

method: Categorical latent mixture (K=4) correlates positions in a block; acceptance-oriented training objective for T>0
upside: joint draft becomes a mixture of products, so positions co-vary; strongest at high entropy
method_downside: only K=4 latent components, so dependence is coarse; trained with a biased surrogate objective and greedy-branch proposals that do not match stochastic inference
accepted_tokens: >12% macro tau gain over DFlash, Qwen3-8B high-entropy (T 0.7-1.5, top-p 0.8/0.95)
speed: not reported

method: Pretrained AR correction heads extended from chains to trees by depth-wise parallel batching and deferred best-first pruning
upside: parent-conditioned node distributions across many branches
method_downside: one correction-head pass per tree depth, so sequential steps grow with depth; tree verify cost grows with nodes x batch
memory: not reported; DFlash drafter + AR correction heads
accepted_tokens: up to 12.97; Qwen3-8B avg 9.81 (T=0, extractor, check)
speed: up to 9.73x; Qwen3-8B avg 6.99x (T=0; GPU not given)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: On-policy distillation of a diffusion drafter with clipped reverse-KL plus adaptive length head
upside: drafter trained on its own rollouts; length head cuts wasted verify slots under load
method_downside: on-policy distillation needs target rollouts per domain; bidirectional in-block attention gives high-variance drafts
memory: not reported; DFlash-size drafter + length head (est.)
accepted_tokens: DFlash baseline tau 7.09 at c=1 (Qwen3-8B); AdaFlash not extracted
speed: up to 5.3x over AR; +66% throughput over prior SOTA at c=128 (SGLang); DFlash 0.90x at c=128
datasets: MathQA, GSM8K, OpenCodeInstruct, CodeAlpaca, ShareGPT, Blend, 2 long reasoning sets

method: Relay module shifts and modulates target hidden states at rejected positions into the next draft; multi-round self-conditioned training
upside: reuses verifier information otherwise discarded, at 1.2% latency
method_downside: block fixed at 16 (accepted length capped); still needs fresh target features each round; training mismatch when combined with Domino
memory: not reported; small MLP relay on DFlash
speed: 2.65x at c=1 down to 1.35x at c=32 (Qwen3-8B, SGLang, A800)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: During verify, precomputes drafts for every acceptance boundary (d+1 anchors, M-DFlash) so drafting fully overlaps verification
upside: hides drafter latency with no fallback round
method_downside: drafter computes d+1=8 anchors per round, multiplying draft compute; needs a dedicated drafting GPU, competing with verify at bs>1
memory: no new params (fine-tuned DSpark checkpoint); extra drafting GPU; ~8x per-round draft activations (est.)
accepted_tokens: not extracted (+30.7% tau from multi-anchor fine-tuning)
speed: 3.21x Qwen3-8B, 3.52x 14B; +11.1%/5.1% vs DSpark (H800, bs1-16, greedy)
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, MBPP, CodeAlpaca, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Block-diffusion drafter with fixed-cost prefix encoding: boundary state, recent window, global summary
upside: draft cost and state stay flat with context (~3.5 ms 1K-128K)
method_downside: fixed-size summary is lossy for far context (rare long-range tokens); needs a dedicated drafter GPU
memory: drafter state 6.3 MiB at 128K (406x smaller than DSpark); one extra drafter GPU
speed: 1.88-2.13x over AR at 1K-128K; 128K TPOT 74.3 vs 97.2 ms DSpark; +6-12% vs DSpark at c=128
datasets: LongSpec (32K), CodeSpan (64K), LongSWE-Bench (128K), Alpaca, MBPP, MATH-500 (8 total)

method: Confidence-Adaptive Token reweighting aligns loss with acceptance; one drafter serves target-dependent (hidden features) and target-independent modes
upside: one drafter for a model family, or higher accuracy when target features are available
method_downside: separate drafter with its own KV growing with context; target-dependent mode needs target features each round; target-independent mode limited to one tokenizer family
memory: not reported; separate small drafter (PARD-style, size not extracted) plus its KV
speed: Qwen3-8B 5.81x vs DFlash 4.61x, PARD 4.39x, EAGLE-3 1.93x (A100-40GB, vLLM, T=0)
llama_results: LLaMA3.1-8B 6.94x / tau 9.19 (vLLM, T=0); notes also cite 5.19x (conflict, check table)

method: LoRA adapter on the target backbone acts as a same-backbone block-diffusion drafter (D=16)
upside: no separate drafter weights
method_downside: draft pass is a full-backbone pass, as expensive as verify (~50 ms each), so tau gains do not pay off
memory: LoRA adapter only; reuses target weights (draft pass costs a full forward)
speed: 34.05 tok/s vs FastMTP 188.01 tok/s (Qwen3-0.6B, bf16, T=0, 256 tokens)

method: NAR 12+2-layer Spec-Drafter drafts k=25 tokens; accept if in target top-β (β=3) and log-prob gap to top-1 ≤ τ (1.0)
upside: relaxed top-β/τ acceptance lets long NAR blocks survive, so ~8 tokens accepted per iteration
method_downside: lossy: output no longer the target's greedy/sampled sequence; β and τ must be tuned per task; separate drafter trained per target (mask-predict)
memory: separate Transformer-base-size drafter; paper reports ~245-555 MB extra at test time
quality: lossy, no drop measured: BLEU 28.93 vs 28.73 AR greedy (WMT14 En-De); ROUGE +0.03 (CNN/DM, BART-base)
speed: 5.1-5.5x (Transformer-base, P100, bs1); 3.0-3.3x (12+2 target); 5.1x (BART-base)

method: small model generates; fallback to large model when small-model confidence is low; rollback when large-model cross-entropy to a small token exceeds a threshold
upside: plug-and-play, no training; tokens with small discrepancy are kept, so the large model runs rarely
method_downside: lossy: tokens the large model would not pick are kept; fallback and rollback thresholds must be tuned; small and large models must be aligned (README advises fine-tuning the small model)
memory: not reported; small model (T5/mT5-small class) + its KV (est.)
quality: lossy: 'minimal' quality degradation at up to 2.12x; exact BLEU/ROUGE drop not seen
speed: up to 2.12x (T4 GPU)
datasets: IWSLT2017 De-En, WMT14 De-En, XSum, CNN/DM

method: decoding heads + tree attention; accept candidate if target prob > min(ε, δ·exp(−H(p))) instead of rejection sampling
upside: entropy-adaptive threshold accepts more candidates at T>0 than rejection sampling, without a separate drafter
method_downside: lossy at T>0: not the target distribution (reduces to greedy match at T=0); ε, δ are global constants to tune; heads retrained per target
memory: Medusa heads: ResBlock + own vocab projection each, ~0.15B per head on 7B, ~0.7B for 5 heads (est.); no extra KV
quality: lossy at T>0: MT-Bench quality roughly unchanged (unv.)
accepted_tokens: not reported for typical acceptance alone
speed: ~2x wall-time (Vicuna-7B/13B/33B, A100, bs1, MT-Bench, Medusa-1); +10% over greedy on creative tasks with typical acceptance; Medusa-2 2.3-3.6x (unv.)

method: choose the output distribution that maximizes acceptance subject to an f-divergence budget (TV/KL) to the target; link to boosting
upside: explicit, provably optimal acceptance-quality trade-off; cheap data structure (O(sort(n)) build, O(log n) query)
method_downside: lossy: output follows a divergence-bounded proxy, not the target; per-token budget compounds over sequence length; budget must be chosen
memory: none beyond the drafter (est.); per-step sort over the vocabulary
quality: lossy with bounded per-token divergence; measured drop not reported in material seen
speed: not reported (full text not read)

method: linear judge head on target last-layer embeddings classifies whether a mismatching draft token is still correct; accept if yes
upside: accepts mismatches that are semantically fine, so ~20 tokens per round with a strong 8B drafter
method_downside: lossy: no guarantee of target distribution; judge needs hand-labeled error annotations and new domains need new labels (OOD drop); needs a strong drafter (Medusa/EAGLE heads unsuitable) and a large target
memory: judge head 16,384 params (405B) / 8,192 (70B), negligible; plus separate Llama-3.1-8B drafter + its KV
quality: lossy: GSM8K ~90% and HumanEval 86.6% ~ target 405B; OOD (code removed from judge data) HumanEval 86.6% -> 80.4%
speed: 8B/405B: 9.7x HF, 3.9x gpt-fast, 129.3 tok/s; 8B/70B: 2x HF, 3x gpt-fast, 141.8 tok/s (H100, 8-bit, bs1)

method: mine 'important' mismatches (substitution changes final answer) offline with target rollouts, train logistic regression on draft+target hidden states, accept unimportant mismatches
upside: removes manual annotation of Judge Decoding; cheap classifier at inference
method_downside: lossy: target distribution not preserved; labels need verifiable tasks (final-answer change) and classifier degrades OOD, so mining is redone per domain; offline mining needs many sequential target passes
memory: logistic regression on concatenated hidden states (~6k params, est.) + Llama-3.2-1B drafter + KV
quality: lossy: ≤1% accuracy drop on GSM8K at ~1.5x more accepted tokens; ~1% drop on LiveCodeBench at ~2x
accepted_tokens: 15+ (GSM8K), 20+ (LiveCodeBench) per cycle, window W=64 (Llama 1B/8B, greedy on GSM8K)
speed: ~2x over standard SD (GSM8K/LiveCodeBench); hardware and batch not specified
llama_results: Llama-3.2-1B -> Llama-3.1-8B: up to 1.5x more accepted tokens at ≤1% GSM8K drop

method: self-supervised judge: label mismatches by semantic preservation score (bidirectional likelihood of replaced vs original token), train logistic regression on target hidden states
upside: no ground-truth answers needed, so labels extend beyond math/code
